The circle at the top vertex contains 7, the circle at the lower-left vertex contains 1, the circle at the lower-right vertex contains 3, and the circle in the middle of the bottom side contains 6. In the middle of each of the left and right slanted sides, there is a circle covered by ink, and the number inside is not visible. Reasoning: The problem says that the sum of the three numbers on each side of the triangle is equal. The three numbers on the bottom side are all visible, so the common sum is 1 + 6 + 3 = 10. Let the number covered on the left slanted side be x, then the sum on the left side is 7 + x + 1 = 10, so x = 2. Let the number covered on the right slanted side be y, then the sum on the right side is 7 + y + 3 = 10, so y = 0. The sum of the two covered numbers is x + y = 2 + 0 = 2.
